goal: Extract the reusable discovery/research node, generation, field, and edge semantics from domainspec-core CANONICAL-KINDS, while distinguishing declared contracts from demonstrated use and drift.
context: Cyberalchemy needs a minimal schema in which every registered node has an identifiable generation process and supported relations. The owner fixes artifact_kind as the single kind field and hypothesizes that users may evolve their own kinds and edges from soft schemas toward categorical composition; the universal invariant candidate is the existence of frontmatter and edges. The first bounded case is the lifecycle from research initial definitions through collected research to findings, before a later research connects micro tasks to macro context. The scouts must bring only source-grounded evidence from the frozen domainspec-core canonical-kind corpus and must not declare a local canonical schema.

groups.anti_bias: composite: methodology and source-corpus - formal/schema reconstruction of normative declarations versus historical/empirical reconstruction of instances, sessions, reviews, and drift

agents.angle: formal/schema reconstruction over CANONICAL-KINDS.md, ALLOWED-EDGES.yaml, EDGES.yaml, the instance-contract session, and the authority review; prioritize declared types, invariants, generators, validators, allowed values, and endpoint constraints
agents.initial_prompt: Read the frozen task context and the specified domainspec-core canonical-kind corpus. Examine BOTH discovery and research. The owner has fixed one local naming constraint: node_type and artifact_kind are the same concept, and the single field is artifact_kind. Treat as a hypothesis, not a conclusion, that users may choose and evolve their own artifact kinds and edges, while the universal invariant is only that registered artifacts have frontmatter and edges; progressively stronger schemas may eventually support categorical types, morphisms, and composition without becoming immutable. Reconstruct the normative contract: what counts as a registered node, what process creates it, which fields exist and who generates them, which values are closed or open, which edges are allowed, which source/target constraints apply, and where authority or validation lives. Separate direct source facts from your interpretation. Identify what is portable to cyberalchemy-orchestrator, what is domainspec-core-specific, and any contradiction with local ontology-conventions.md. Write only research/research-lifecycle-definitions/evidence/canonical-kinds-normative-scout.md. Every load-bearing statement must cite an exact source path and selector or line. Do not edit sources and do not declare a canonical local schema. Return a concise handoff naming the file, strongest reusable elements, and blockers.
